title: Tail-capture workload suite + golden lockfile for deterministic CI perf gates
creator: Diego Ramos
description:
Goal:
Deliver a new deterministic benchmark harness and workload suite ("tail-capture") that better reflects long-tail production traffic for kernel selection, attention-optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling. Produce a human-auditable golden lockfile format (readable TOML-style) that CI can pin against and update via a controlled approval flow.

Problem Statement:
Current golden baselines are too coarse and sensitive to nondeterministic noise (GPU scheduling, tiny kernel variation) which leads to flaky CI perf gates. Kernel routing and prefill/decode pacing changes often generate transient p99 regressions that are hard to triage because we lack: 1) tail-focused workloads, 2) deterministic noise injection for signal calibration, and 3) an auditable golden file with cohort metadata and hardware topology fingerprints.

Success Criteria:
- New tail-capture workload set reproduces 95th-99.9th percentile shapes seen in production traces (based on replay sample).
- Golden lockfile format captures: workload cohort id, canonical seed list, hardware fingerprint (GPU model + topology), kernel-matrix expected costs, and baseline latency/throughput vectors.
- CI perf gates use a rolling-window comparison (3 golden runs) with adaptive thresholds to reduce false positives by >=50% versus current gates while preserving sensitivity to true regressions.
- Automatable approval flow: when a suggested golden update is produced, it creates a PR and a staged canary run before requiring product/rls owner sign-off.

Approach/Plan:
1) Build tail-capture workload generator (benchserver plugin) that:
   - ingests lightweight production trace samples (privacy-scrubbed),
   - synthesizes cohorts for short/medium/long tokens, multi-turn chat, and attention-window hotspots,
   - outputs deterministic seeds and request-metadata used by the runner.
2) Implement deterministic noise-injection layer to calibrate bench stability (controlled jitter in microbatch arrival, tiny CPU scheduling offsets) so golden tolerances can be measured.
3) Design golden lockfile schema (TOML-like, human readable) which includes cohort metadata, kernel matrix expectations, and hardware fingerprint. Lockfile is stored in a git-managed golden repo.
4) Extend CI: perf-checker action that runs 3 golden runs (cold, warm-KV, hot-cache) and computes p50/p95/p99 deltas and an SLO-weighted regression score. If score exceeds threshold, fail; otherwise open a suggested-update PR.
5) Kernel selection matrix: run cross-product of candidate kernels across representative cohorts and capture compatibility/quality flags; surface as CSV attached to lockfile.
6) Small rollout: limit initial gate to runtime branches with the new bench agent enabled; monitor false-positive rate for 2 cycles before broadening.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Running 3 golden runs increases CI minutes; mitigate by running on Dedicated bench pool and caching model artifacts.
- Deterministic injection may not emulate all production noise; we'll keep production trace replay as an additional check for major rollouts.
- Hardware fingerprint granularity: vendor+model vs full topology. Start coarse and expand if needed.

Acceptance Criteria (for Done):
- Benchserver plugin merged and docs in Confluence (link below).
- Golden lockfile schema committed in runtime-bench/goldens repo with at least 5 cohort lockfiles.
- CI perf-checker integrated and gating enabled on one protected branch with runbook entries.
- Telemetry dashboard showing false-positive and true-regression rates for the new gates.

Artifacts & Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/789012345/Tail-Capture+Benchmark+Design
- Implementation PR (runtime bench): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2134
- Goldens repo (example lockfile): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/tree/main/goldens
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ayesha Kapoor: Kickoff complete. Collected 72k anonymized trace samples. Initial cohort sketch attached to the Confluence doc.

2025-02-24 - Diego Ramos: Prototype of deterministic generator merged to feature/bench-tail. Observed high variance on p99 with default kernels on A100-80GB; added deterministic jitter to bench harness to stabilize runs.
2025-02-27 - PM review (Nina Chen): Please ensure the golden update PR triggers a canary run and not auto-merge. Product owners want a human approval step for baseline shifts >2% on p99.
2025-03-01 - Eng review (Marcus Li): Kernel matrix CSV looks good. Decided to start with model-class fingerprint (e.g., A100-80GB v3) rather than per-card topology to reduce file churn.
2025-03-03 - QA (Rohit Patel): Ran three golden cycles against dedicated bench pool. False positives down ~57% in this sample. Filing follow-up to measure across more hardware.
2025-03-04 - Ayesha Kapoor: Opened impl PR for CI perf-checker action: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/pull/98. Next: wire approval flow and canary run orchestration.
